main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling fried salted fish in the shared kitchen, given smell affecting others' rooms, work calls and laundry

A-B.evidence: B backed A's no-smelly-food request (T2), later said the time doesn't matter and accepted a heads-up (T13, T21). A accepted a weekend once-a-week plan (T16). They never addressed each other directly, and both ended with D's plan.

A-C.evidence: C echoed A's complaint (T3, T7), then objected to the timing and accepted advance notice of the weekend day (T14, T25, T29). A accepted the once-weekly weekend plan (T16). They did not speak to each other.

A-D.evidence: A moved from a ban on strong smells (T1) to timing-only (T9); D accepted after 7pm and checking first (T10-11). Both agreed to once a week on weekends (T15-16).

B-C.evidence: B and C echoed each other's complaints (T6-7, T13-14, T17-18). Both ended up accepting advance notice from D (T21, T25).

B-D.evidence: B objected that timing doesn't help and that the smell fills the room (T13, T17). D asked what B wants (T19). B offered to close the door if told beforehand (T21), and D agreed to give notice (T22, T26).

C-D.evidence: C said the weekend still affects the laundry (T18). D asked C about laundry (T22). C proposed being told which day (T25) and D agreed (T26). C said 'works for me' (T29).
